user.title: Unavailable-Aware Triggers
user.description: Adds `unavailable_aware.state` and `unavailable_aware.numeric_state` triggers to the automation editor.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Unavailable-Aware Triggers is already set up.

state.name: State (unavailable-aware)
state.description: Triggers when an entity's state or attribute changes, seeing through unavailable, unknown, and removed. Dropping out and coming back unchanged does not fire; a real change while unavailable does.

attribute.name: Attribute
attribute.description: Trigger on this attribute instead of the state.

from.name: From
from.description: Only trigger when it changes from one of these values. After a gap, this is the value before the gap.

not_from.name: Not from
not_from.description: Only trigger when it changes from a value not in this list. After a gap, this is the value before the gap.

to.name: To
to.description: Only trigger when it changes to one of these values.

not_to.name: Not to
not_to.description: Only trigger when it changes to a value not in this list.

for.name: For
for.description: Only trigger once the new state has held for this long.

bridge_up_to.name: Bridge gaps up to
bridge_up_to.description: Gaps up to this long are bridged: coming back unchanged does not fire, and a real change while unavailable is compared to the state before the gap.

longer_gaps.name: Longer gaps
longer_gaps.description: What happens when the entity comes back after a gap longer than `Bridge gaps up to`, or with no earlier state to compare against. Ignore is the safe choice: the change may have happened at any point while it was away. Home Assistant default does what Home Assistant's own trigger would, so coming back unchanged after a long gap fires too.

bridge_restarts_for_timer.name: Bridge restarts For timer
bridge_restarts_for_timer.description: With `For:`, what a bridged gap does to the timer when the entity comes back unchanged. Off: the gap doesn't interrupt the timer. On: the timer starts over (Home Assistant default behavior).

numeric_state.name: Numeric state (unavailable-aware)
numeric_state.description: Triggers when a value enters a range, seeing through unavailable, unknown, and removed. Whether the value was already in range is determined from the state before a gap.

attribute.name: Attribute
attribute.description: Trigger on this attribute instead of the state.

above.name: Above
above.description: Trigger when the value rises above this.

below.name: Below
below.description: Trigger when the value drops below this.

for.name: For
for.description: Only trigger once the new state has held for this long.

bridge_up_to.name: Bridge gaps up to
bridge_up_to.description: Gaps up to this long are bridged: coming back unchanged does not fire, and a real change while unavailable is compared to the state before the gap.

Ignore is the safe choice: the change may have happened at any point while it was away. Home Assistant default does what Home Assistant's own trigger would, so coming back unchanged after a long gap fires too.

bridge_restarts_for_timer.name: Bridge restarts For timer
bridge_restarts_for_timer.description: With `For:`, what a bridged gap does to the timer when the entity comes back unchanged. Off: the gap doesn't interrupt the timer. On: the timer starts over (Home Assistant default behavior).

options.home_assistant_default: Home Assistant default: fire as Home Assistant's built-in trigger would, treating the change as coming from unavailable or unknown
